definitions.explanation: The electrical potential difference between two points, measured in volts. A fundamental concept in electricity and electronics.

examples.japanese: {日本|にほん}の{家庭|かてい}の{電圧|でんあつ}は100ボルトだ。
examples.english: The household voltage in Japan is 100 volts.

examples.japanese: {海外|かいがい}で{日本|にほん}の{電化製品|でんかせいひん}を{使|つか}うときは、{電圧|でんあつ}の{違|ちが}いに{注意|ちゅうい}が{必要|ひつよう}だ。
examples.english: When using Japanese electronics overseas, you need to be careful about voltage differences.

notes:
A compound of {電|でん} (electricity) and {圧|あつ} (pressure). The standard term for voltage in both everyday and technical contexts.

CULTURAL NOTE:
Japan uses 100V household electricity, which is lower than most countries (110-240V). This is a common topic for travelers and expats who need voltage converters ({変圧器|へんあつき}).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {電圧|でんあつ}が{高|たか}い/{低|ひく}い — high/low voltage
- {電圧|でんあつ}を{上|あ}げる/{下|さ}げる — to raise/lower voltage
- {高|こう}{電圧|でんあつ} — high voltage
- {電圧|でんあつ}{変換|へんかん} — voltage conversion

RELATED WORDS:
- {電流|でんりゅう} — electric current
- {電力|でんりょく} — electric power
- {変圧器|へんあつき} — transformer, voltage converter
- ボルト — volt (unit)
